newsitem.title: USA: US may decide on Lebanon travel ban in 20-30 days.
newsitem.headline: US may decide on Lebanon travel ban in 20-30 days.

text.p: The United States could decide whether to lift its long-standing travel ban on Lebanon in 20 to 30 days, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Monday.

Secretary of State Warren Christopher made no mention of the travel ban at a "Friends of Lebanon" meeting at the State Department, but Burns said later the matter would be "under very active review" during Christopher's last month in office.

"We have a serious commitment to make sure we give the best advice we can to the American public which would travel to Lebanon," Burns told reporters. "I think you'll probably hear more from us on this in the next 20 to 30 days.
"I can't tell you if it will be positive or negative but there will be a point where we have to review it one more time before the secretary leaves office," Burns said.
Christopher's last day is likely to be Jan. 20, the second inaugural for President Bill Clinton. His nominated successor is current U.S. United Nations envoy Madeleine Albright.

Washington insists that its ban on U.S. citizens travelling to Lebanon is a security matter dating back to the seizure of American hostages by pro-Iranian groups there in the 1980s. But Beirut suspects it is being used as a bargaining chip to force it into signing a peace treaty with Israel.
